relevance_note: The paper describes a mother and daughter with a TNFAIP3 variant: 'a heterozygous NM_001270508.2: c.608T > G, p.(Leu203Arg) missense variant of TNFAIP3 in both patients'.
method_note: Written by hand with a small Python builder; Table 1 has patients as rows (P1, P2), and P1's row is split over two Markdown lines, so P1 spans use the text or single cells. No stacked ' / ' cells. Labels: the paper uses 'P1'/'P2' (Table 1, figures) and 'Patient 1'/'Patient 2' in text; 'P1'/'P2' chosen as most frequent. In scope also: 'brother of P1' (pedigree legend: deceased at 40, rheumatism and thyroid disease; not tested) and 'L001', a CVID patient control with a TNFAIP3 LoF variant c.1309del (p.Ala437Profs) used only as a functional comparator (no other individual details; included because the scope rule covers every described person with a TNFAIP3 variant). Left out: the mother's heterozygous TNFRSF13B c.310T > C (p.Cys104Arg), which the authors call a known risk factor (risk alleles are excluded by the rules). Inheritance for P2 recorded as inherited maternal because the paper states the mother (P1) carries the same variant ('in both patients'); P1's parents are not described. Possible inconsistencies: Table 1 gives P1's age at onset as '18 years' while the text reports a childhood history of oral and genital ulcers; Table 1 gives P2's onset as '9 years' while the text says ulcers 'since adolescence'. Table 1 therapies (P1 methotrexate, IgRT; P2 anakinra, golimumab) are not mentioned in the text. P1's iliac occlusion on CT was 'without features typical of vasculitis', but a skin biopsy showed leucocytoclastic vasculitis; these are different sites, so vasculitis is kept observed. Ages at presentation (P1 49 years, P2 29 years) are not recorded as last evaluation or diagnosis ages; diagnoses of RA at 18 (P1) and ITP at 29 (P2) are recorded as feature onsets, not age at HA20 diagnosis. Checklist judgements: P1 gastroenteritis with high fever not counted as GI inflammation or recurrent fever; P1 leukopenia not called autoimmune, so cytopenia (autoimmune) left not reported; P1 purpura counted as a skin lesion; P2 'no signs of insulin deficiency' not used to exclude type 1 diabetes; P2 diarrhea not counted as GI inflammation; the brother's 'rheumatism' and 'thyroid disease' are too unspecific for the checklist. Normal C3/C4 recorded as excluded 'low complement' (D-27).

span: P1: 0.205; P2 0.218; L001 0.453 versus mean ratio HC:0.802
The expression levels of A20 in D001 (patient 1) and D002 (patient 2) were reduced compared to HCs
Overexpression of this missense A20 variant in HEK293T enhanced NF-κB signaling, reflected by increased TRAF6 expression and IκBα phosphorylation.
Patient-derived PBMCs demonstrated reduced A20 expression, increased phosphorylation within the NF-κB, STAT1, and mTOR pathways, and elevated production of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
